lesson.title: M8 · Kernel SVM on non-separable data
lesson.lead: Priority 4. 10 marks: 2023 regular Q2A (1-D data, 5), 2023 DS regular Q3B (XOR, 5). Saurabh sir's biggest group: 8 problems.

blocks.label: Before this
blocks.text: M6 and M7 (kernels), and M3 (the dual and f(x) = Σαᵢyᵢk(xᵢ, x) + b).

**They give:** data that no straight line separates (alternating points on a line, XOR corners, inner and outer rings). **They ask:** show it is not linearly separable, pick a kernel or φ, find the boundary, and map it back to the original space.

items: Show no line works (e.g. XOR: each class sits on a diagonal).
Choose φ: x → (x, x²) for 1-D data; x₁x₂ for XOR; (xᵀz + 1)² for rings.
Solve the SVM in feature space (often by symmetry, or with the dual).
Write f(x) = Σ αᵢ yᵢ k(xᵢ, x) + b and set f(x) = 0 to get the boundary in the original space: two thresholds, the axes, a circle or a hyperbola.
Classify new points by the sign of f(x).

Saurabh sir: **P49** (axis-pattern data, homogeneous quadratic kernel), **P50** (bias and boundary, non-homogeneous kernel), **P52** (XOR), **Practice Paper Q7** (kernel SVM on a line, 5M), **Companion Q1** (XNOR), **Q2** (inner/outer rings), **Q5** (1-D, two thresholds), **Q17** (choose the kernel).
**Read:** SVM Companion §11.3–11.4 and §11.8–11.9 (no straight line, the kernel trick, putting the kernel in the SVM, **the exam recipe**).
**Do:** Practice Paper Q7, P52 (XOR), Companion Q1, Q2, Q5, then 2023 Q2A and 2023 DS Q3B.
**Video, only if stuck:** Reuse StatQuest Part 2 from M7 if needed. Skip Part 3 (RBF): never asked in an MFML paper.

worked.title: Kernels · 2023 Q2A: the kernel trick on 1-D data (5 marks)

problem.text: Positive class: (7, 0), (9, 0). Negative class: (8, 0), (10, 0). Use the kernel trick: find a suitable φ(x) and the decision boundary.

steps.label: Why a line fails
steps.text: On the x-axis the labels alternate +, −, +, − (7, 8, 9, 10). No single threshold separates them.

steps.label: Boundary
steps.text: In feature space the classes sit at 1 and 0, so the boundary is **φ = 0.5** (midway) [2M].

steps.label: Alternative
steps.text: φ(x) = cos(πx) also works: −1 for odd x, +1 for even x, boundary cos(πx) = 0. Any φ that separates the parities gets the marks if justified.

worked.answer: φ(x) = x mod 2; boundary at 0.5 in feature space (odd x → +, even x → −).

worked.title: Kernels · 2023 DS regular Q3B: XOR data with (4 + xᵀz)² (5 marks)

problem.text: (2, 2) +, (−2, −2) +, (2, −2) −, (−2, 2) −. (i) Is it linearly separable? [1M] (ii) Derive a suitable kernel matrix. [1.5M] (iii) Derive the SVM decision boundary. [2.5M]

steps.label: (i)
steps.text: No: each class sits on one diagonal of the square (XOR pattern), so no straight line separates them.

steps.label: (ii) Kernel
steps.text: Use K(x, z) = (4 + xᵀz)². xᵀz = 8 for a point with itself, −8 for the opposite corner of the same class, 0 for the other class ⇒ K = 144 on the diagonal, 16 everywhere else.

steps.label: (iii) Dual
steps.text: Maximise Σαᵢ − ½ΣΣαᵢαⱼyᵢyⱼKᵢⱼ. Setting the derivatives to 0 gives four equations such as 144α₁ + 16α₂ − 16α₃ − 16α₄ = 1. By symmetry all αᵢ are equal: **αᵢ = 1/128**.

steps.label: (iii) Boundary
steps.text: The x₁x₂ feature carries all the weight (w = (0, 0, 22.6, 0, 0, 0) in the key's feature order), b = 0. So the boundary is **x₁x₂ = 0**: the two axes. Points with x₁x₂ > 0 are +, x₁x₂ < 0 are −.

worked.answer: Not linearly separable; K = 144 diagonal, 16 elsewhere; αᵢ = 1/128; boundary x₁x₂ = 0.

worked.title: Kernels · Practice Paper Q7: kernel SVM on a line (5 marks)

problem.text: x = −2 (+1), x = 0 (−1), x = 2 (+1); K(x, z) = (xz + 1)². (a) Kernel matrix. [1M] (b) With α₁ = α₃ = a, use Σαᵢyᵢ = 0 and yᵢf(xᵢ) = 1 to find a, α₂ and b. [2M] (c) Show f(x) = ½x² − 1 and give the thresholds. [1M] (d) Classify x = 1 and x = −3. [1M]

flashcards.back: f(x) = Σαᵢyᵢk(xᵢ, x) + b; classify by its sign.

quiz.q: Labels on a line alternate +, −, +, − at x = 7, 8, 9, 10. A suitable φ?
quiz.explain: x mod 2 sends odd x to 1 and even x to 0; x and x² keep the order, so they still alternate.
